item.subject: maths
item.stem:
The diagram shows quadrilateral $ABCD$ with diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ meeting at $O$. Sia already knows the diagonals are equal and bisect each other, as in a rectangle. She asks what extra diagonal condition makes $ABCD$ a square.

Which claim is correct?

options.A: The diagonals also meet at right angles at $O$, so $ABCD$ is a square.
options.B: Call the figure a diagonal construction and treat that label alone as the square test.
options.C: Meeting at right angles is what produces equal diagonals that bisect each other.
options.D: Treat $ABCD$ as a kite whose one symmetry diagonal alone settles the square test.
